value: Sequence as found. Oct 1860: burned; masonry stood 'more imposing' than timber halls (S02 p.176). 1873: stood enough for Ohlmer and Child. Repairs under Tongzhi stopped 1874 (S838). 1900: 'Boxers and other looters broke into the Yuan Ming Yuan', timber pulled down (S02 p.209). Wang Huaiqing as gendarmerie chief used what he wanted for his garden and let carters haul brick and stone 'especially ... the foreign buildings' (S02 p.198). Mid-1920s to 1930s: stone went to houses in the city. 1970s: stone moved to institutions (S817). 1980-85: cleared, stones not all put back right (S821). 1977-92: conservation, maze rebuilt (see row)
